headline: Fresh graduates in India are finding entry-level tech jobs harder to get as AI automates routine work.
score_reason: Pool 6; a trend feature with figures from named firms and analysts; no stale or overstatement finding.
importance_line: Entry-level hiring is slowing at India's bank and tech hubs, which affects new graduates first and then the hubs and the banks, and the doubt is that the feature itself finds little evidence yet of mass job losses.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by The Economic Times, that new graduates in India are struggling to find entry-level jobs at Global Capability Centers, the offices where global firms run tech and back-office work, as AI automates routine tasks. Citigroup has hired a net 2,000 people in India this year, down from about 4,000 last year, and the report finds little evidence yet of mass job losses at these hubs.
